subject.title: RFC: Readiness Conditions and Standard Hosting Profiles

question: Should OpenClaw accept canonical readiness conditions first and defer standard profiles and provider APIs, or adopt the entire combined support contract now?
rationale: The document is coherent and its prior compatibility defect is fixed, but only maintainers can commit OpenClaw to permanent runtime, configuration, plugin API, release-gate, and hosting-support boundaries.

options.title: Accept incrementally
options.body: Approve canonical conditions, unchanged unset-profile behavior, and legacy projections first, then review profiles and provider APIs as later commitments.

options.title: Accept the full RFC
options.body: Approve all four profiles, provider registration, operator composition, and release conformance together after complete runtime and upgrade proof.

options.title: Pause the direction
options.body: Keep the RFC in draft if core-owned hosting profiles and readiness-provider APIs are not a current product priority.

recommendation.title: Accept incrementally
recommendation.body: Approve canonical conditions, unchanged unset-profile behavior, and legacy projections first, then review profiles and provider APIs as later commitments.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the repository's RFC lifecycle and template, making them the strongest history-backed owner for the acceptance-process decision.
